Militia: cost 1 Food (+0 to combat)
Guard: cost 1 Food and 1 Weapon, upkeep 1 Food (+1 to combat) 
Troop: cost 1 Food, 1 Weapon, and 1 Wealth; upkeep 1 Food (+2 to combat)
Veteran: cost 1 Food, 2 Loyalty, and 2 Wealth; upkeep 1 Food (+3 to combat)
Knight: cost 1 Food, Horse, Wealth, and 2 Weapon; upkeep 1 Wealth and Food (+4 to combat)
Adventurers: cost at least 1 Wealth; will explore or clear hexes and leave at the end of the year (+1 to combat per Wealth paid)

--Militias may be levied from each Population at the cost of 1 Loyalty lost from overall Governance Stats when doing so outside of defensive purposes.

--Wooden fortifications give a unit +1 to their combat rolls when defending inside, while stone fortifications give a unit +2 when defending inside (for settlement walls, forts, castles, temporary camps)

content:
BUILDINGS

MAIN SETTLEMENT
Town Hall: houses 2 Population/Units, central building, gives 1 Diplomacy
    Costs 1 Wood to build, Costs 1 designated Resource as tax per year
Homes: houses 2 Population/Units so that Unrest doesn’t go up due to homeless
    Costs 1 Wood to build
Manor: houses 1 Population and important PCs/NPCs, can be a town's central building, gives 1 Loyalty
    Costs 1 Wood and 1 Wealth to build
Stables: gives 1 Horse, 1 on 1d4 adds 1 Horse each year
    Costs 1 Wood to build, upkeep of 1 Food per year
Tavern: will generate 1 Wealth per year, gives 1 Intrigue
    Costs 1 Wood to build, upkeep of 1 Food per year
Market: can exchange 1 of a resource for 1 Wealth each per month, or v.versa if needed
    Costs 1 Wood and 1 Wealth to build
Trade Post: can exchange 1 of a resource for 1 Wealth and v.versa yearly per trade partner
    Costs 1 Wood and 2 Wealth to build, Cost 1 Horse or 1 Ship when forming trade partner
Merchant Guild: generates 1 Wealth and Diplomacy yearly, allows one yearly bulk exchange of one resource
    Costs 2 Wood and 3 Wealth to build, requires Trade Post, Artisan Shop, and Market
Shrine: gives 1 Piety
    Costs 1 Wood or 1 Stone to build
Temple: gives 1 Piety, can exchange 1 Wealth for 1 Piety per year, quells 1 Unrest per year
    Costs 1 Wood, 1 Stone, 1 Wealth to build 
Schools 1 on 1d4 generates 1 Loyalty, attempts once a year
    Costs 1 Wood and 1 Wealth to build
Library request tomes, 1 on 1d4 generates 1 Diplomacy, attempts once a year
    Costs 2 Wood and 1 Wealth to build, upkeep 1 Wealth per year
University 1 on 1d4 generates 1 Diplomacy, 1 Loyalty, and 1 Piety, attempts once a year
    Costs 2 Wood, 1 Stone, and 2 Wealth to build, upkeep 1 Wealth per year; requires School and Library
Smithy can exchange 1 Iron to create 1 Weapon or 1 Tool monthly
    Costs 1 Wood to build
Gallows includes pillories and cages, gives 1 Dread
    Costs 1 Wood to build
Spy Quarters gives 1 Intrigue and 1 Dread, 1 on 1d6 gives 2 Intrigue and 1 Dread yearly
    Costs 1 Wood, 1 Stone, and 2 Loyalty to build
Embassies gives 1 Diplomacy, can exchange 1 Wealth for 1 Diplomacy each year per ally
    Costs 2 Wood and 2 Wealth to build
Messenger Post allows fast communication to and from regions via road, even to unexplored settlements
    Costs 1 Wood, 1 Wealth, and 1 Horse to build
Roads creates stretch of road for travel, allows trade to adjoining region
    Costs 1 Tool for 3 hexes with 1 Wood if building through difficult terrain, builds in 1 month
Bridge allows road to span over a river, either made of wood or stone
    Costs 2 Wood OR 2 Stone to build, decrease by 1 at suitable crossing
Ferry allows boats to help large groups cross river
    Costs 2 Wood
Shipyard set up on water, allows for 1 Wood and 1 Wealth to be used to build 1 Ship
    Costs 2 Wood to build
Harbor set up on water, can exchange 1 Ship for 2 of a resource yearly, 1 on 1d4 gives 1 Ship
    Costs 1 Wood, 1 Stone, 1 Tools, 1 Wealth to build, requires Shipyard and Fishing Dock
.
.
RESOURCES
Farm: generates 1 Food each year
    Costs 1 Wood to build
Mill: each farm generates +50% Food each year, non-stacking per settlement
    Costs 1 Wood to build
Artisan Shops: 1 on 1d4 to generate 1 Wealth per year
    Costs 1 Wood and 1 Wealth to build
Hunting Grounds: set up near forest or mountain, generates 1 Food each year
    Costs 1 Wood to build
Logging Camp: set up near forest, generates 1 Wood each year
    Costs 1 Wood to build
Fishing Dock: set up on water, generates 1 Food each year
    Costs 1 Wood to build
Mine: set up on mountain, generates 1 Iron per year
    Costs 1 Wood, 1 Stone, and 1 Tools to build
Silver/Gold Mine: set up on mountain, generates either 1 Wealth (silver) or 2 Wealth (gold) per year
    Costs 1 Wood, 1 Stone, and 1 Tools to build
Quarry: set up near or on mountain, generates 1 Stone per year
    Costs 1 Wood and 1 Tools to build
Herbalist Hut: set up near forest, generates 1 Medicine every year
    Costs 1 Wood to build
Apothecary: gives 1 Medicine, can exchange 1 Wealth for 1 Medicine yearly
    Costs 1 Wood to build, requires 1 Herbalist Hut
Ranch: will create 1 Horse per year
    Costs 1 Wood and 1 Wealth to build, upkeep of 2 Food per year
.
.
DEFENSE and MILITARY
Tower: generates 1 Militia that will defend distance of 3 Tiles
    Costs 1 Stone and 1 Wood to build
Barracks: houses and can create up to 3 Guard/Troops that will defend settlement and realm
    Costs 1 Wood to build, upkeep of 1 Wealth per year
Training Yard: allows for upgrading any military Unit using retrospective resources
    Costs 1 Wood and 1 Wealth to build
Prison: holds captured humanoids, heightened escape DCs added by assigned unit and walls
    Costs 1 Stone and 1 Iron to build
Scout’s Nest: 1 on 1d6 to add 1 Intrigue yearly, reveals potential threats or sites in 4 Tiles
    Costs 2 Wood to build, must be on difficult terrain
Wooden Wall: builds in 3 months, defends hexes from minor raids and danger
    Costs 6 Wood per hex
Stone Wall: builds in 2 years, better defense for hexes from larger dangers
    Costs 6 Stone per hex
Fort: can station Units to defend distance of 4 Tiles, functions like Manor, gives 1 Loyalty
    Costs 4 Wood and 1 Wealth to build
Castle: can station Units to defend distance of 4 Tiles, functions like Manor, gives 1 Loyalty
    Costs 4 Stone and 2 Wealth to build, builds in 2 year or 1 if building on Fort
Adventurer’s Guild: can hire Adventurer Units using 1 Wealth for effectiveness, up to 5.
    Costs 2 Wood, 3 Diplomacy, and 3 Wealth to build

author: The DM
content:
Taxes: 1 Wealth OR 2 of any one resource that you choose
Tithes: 1 Wealth (optional)

Taxes, different from Tithes, are either 1 Wealth OR 2 of any resource you choose per settlement and paid annually. This is because the tax in the form of coin is valued more, but lumps of resources are still accepted.

And don't worry about the "per settlement" part yet. You guys currently have smaller offshoot areas like the quarry or lumber camps, but those aren't settlements even if a few people live there. It's for if you guys get big, go across the lake or something, and decide to build a second castle/townhall/manor with it's own name and local leaders and such. A new settlement like that would factor into the tax further increasing by 1 Wealth/2 Resource.

The taxes are also subject to being increased or decreased, either during times of crisis or some other form of arguably justifiable agreement.

IMPORTANTLY, Tithes are optional. You can pay 1 Wealth per year to have religious clerics of established churches (Pelor, Bahamut, Abadar, Erastil, etc) in the kingdoms to get a presence in your town, teaching and healing and providing services to the people. Doing so increases Piety by 1 each year, and roleplay-wise if you have good relations with them, that religious group can possibly go to bat for you politically if needed.

author: The DM
content:
Here is a basic summary of the region of the world we'll be in (it is all homebrew and new, none of it related to our last campaign).

It is set in a region known as the Free Kingdoms, a temperate part of a larger continent. This region also borders a sea to the north, called the Norean Sea. There are large empires to the south, a ways off the map. There is a frigid and small northern continent off the map, above the Norean Sea. Anything off map generally won't factor too much into the plot. AND, if you invent a place, I'll do what I can to put it somewhere on the map and integrate it into the world.

On the map, we will be starting in the city of Arnestal, in the county of the same name, of the Kingdom of Casdenia. You can choose to be from Arnestal, or have traveled there from one of its neighboring kingdoms (two of which are on the map, two off the map). The main focus of this campaign is on the titular expanse of territory known as the Wilderlands. There will be map exploration, so you can't see the overall map from the get-go.

NOTE: This game is loosely based off the Pathfinder: Kingmaker adventure module and CRPG. The goal is to settle a wilderness, explore its secrets, and see a realm be built -- whether you want to rule or support a ruler or simply live there as others rule, it's up to you. I've majorly simplified the governance mechanics of that module...because they are crazy complex. That being said, I fell in love with the Pathfinder world because of Kingmaker. This isn't that setting, but it was just that enjoyable, so I hope this'll be a fun way to share the experience.

author: weduhman
content:
Travel Notes from 7/22 Session  - 4 Days Total
Our party joins the County sponsored wagon train with 400 other travelers to journey into the Wilderlands. This is a mix of locals from Arnestal, its surrounding villages, travelers from the North, adventures, and in our case, a vagabond 🌿
The caravan travels South then West, through the mountains near Hornstead where we are wrongfully tolled to pass. A confrontation occurs where Hornstead sleezebag Orbin is intimidated into returning the wrongfully collected dues. 🪙  This earns us the approval of wagon members Erik & co. and reveals a lack of leadership from The Warded Protectors, chiefly Caravan Master Gedry (read the fine print, dude!). Guard Sergeant Frey is young and, at first glance, inexperienced.
History warns of aggressive Orc activity in the region. We're told of the Green Skin Wars at a traveler's rest. Other settlers and tradesman have attempted to journey our path, never to return. We are unsure if the two events are related. ⚔️

author: weduhman
content:
Travel Notes from 8/12 Session -  Day 14 
The party officially enters the Wilderlands! The Warded Protectors are divided on whether or not to spend resources on delayed members of the caravan. Gedry and Frey are willing to send guards and slow pace to ensure no one is left behind, while Landar and Tatartius are eager to settle as quickly as possible, even if it means stragglers are on their own. 🐂 
The caravan crosses a creek that results in Erik's wagon sustaining immobilizing damage. Rather than leave our friend, his wife, and their two young children, the party stays back to assist, enlisting the watch of two willing guards. In the middle of repairs, the group is stalked and attacked by four wolves. It is somewhat unusual in the daytime and with so many humanoids around. We sustain no casualties 🐺 
When confronted with the consequences of leaving families and stragglers behind, Landar and Tatartius are unmoved. 
A paid scouting expedition is launched and the party enlists. Our group invites the help of rugged Ranger Echon and two elven kin. Of the four possible scouting sights, the party investigates the Shores of Silverstep and the Gnarl Marches. 
The Shores of Silverstep offers good fishing by land or vessel, though may be a storm coast in inclement weather. It seems like a spot that may attract Water Fey, but whether they are friend or foe is yet to be seen. Legend has it the shore is the footprint of a Silver Dragon 🐉 And where there's a dragon, there's a hoard...
The Gnarl Marches are prime for logging with densely packed trees and access to the river. It is obvious that the Gnarl periodically floods, resulting in rich soil but precarious footing. The lush environment is ideal for hunting (and being hunted) 🏹 
Two locations are left scouted to other groups: The Hills to the North and the Argent River Bank. 
Unease runs through the camp as the party returns from the scouting mission. To our shock and surprise, Caravan Master Gedry lie dead in his tent! ☠️

author: weduhman
content:
Travel Notes from 8/29 Session -  to end of Day 14 
Kaelen and Anora begin investigating Caravan Master Gedry’s murder, performing rites at the scene and noting the cause of death was a slit throat with no signs of struggle. 🔪
Sergeant Frey doubts council involvement, but Tartartius casts blame on new arrivals from the south: Gale the Elven smith, a gnome couple, and a Tiefling. To keep them from leaving, the not-so-Warded Protectors lock down the camp. ⛺
The lockdown angers members like Erik and Torrik, who want to resume trade and settlement efforts. The party faces a dilemma: hold everyone in camp or risk unrest. 🔍
Interrogations follow: Gale is ruled out, but Tartartius publicly accuses the Tiefling thief. Mischievous but not violent, the Tiefling is defended by Aldis who secures a deal - close the case by sundown in exchange for lifting the lockdown. ⏰
Before leaving with his kin, Echon investigates and confirms the murder was the work of a professional, with no tracks in or out of Gedry’s tent. The focus shifts squarely back to the Council.
Frenjamin and Aldis search Tartartius’ tent while Anora and Kaelen question him; no motive or proof surfaces, though suspicion lingers. Landar is also interrogated but offers little beyond self-interest.
With no solid evidence, both the party and the council agree to settle the matter the evening and increase guard patrol for the time being. As luck would have it, the increased patrol saves the Caravan when they ambushed just hours later by bandits and none other than Echon's Elvin kin who accompanied us on the scouting expedition. 🧝‍♂️
We manage to save both Landar and Tartartius from the bandits, and arrive just in time to spare Frey who is on the brink of a major injury. Echon is nowhere to be seen, but a ring is recovered with the symbol of a raven and lyre.
In recognition of their efforts, the party is invited to join the Council. ⚖️

author: weduhman
content:
Settlers Notes from 9/28 Session - to start of day 19 (?)
The Council convenes it's first meeting, sharing news from both expeditions. 🤝
Kaelen and Anora recount defeating the riverside bandits, rescuing Echon, and seizing boats. 🛶
Frenjamin and Aldis report on the decrepit tower: glowing orbs, the un-well, quarry potential, and possible wolves.
The council moves to new business, including Tartartius' request to begin building a bridge to the west. The vote is passed unanimously. Landar requests a manor be  queued and the council tables the idea until a wealth generating resource can be settled upon.
The council motions to vote on clensing the tower to the north, with five-ayes to one-nay. One vote absent. The motion passes and the group sets off with caravan sponsored ponies.
In small group discussion, Aldis shares the map she found in Tartartius tent indicating both potential danger and treasure west of the river. Perhaps this is his true motive for building the bridge. 🗺️
The inner circle sets out for the northern tower and thoroughly investigates the un-well during the daytime. Underground, Kaelen, Anora, and Frenjamin find a broken scepter but cannot identify it's make or power.
The group rests until nighttime, waiting for the un-well to respond as it had before. Come 3:00 am, Kaelen and Anora descend to find a ghost warning them of trespassing in this place.
Franjamin, under the influence of herb, provokes a will-o-wisp which shocks him. Aldis comes to his aid, only for both to flee; one down the well and the other beyond the tower.
Kaelen is downed and Anora becomes possessed; all the ghastly workings of the spirit. 👻
Disturbingly, the puppeteered Anora attacks the descending Frenjamin who is able to revive Kaelen. With power too great, Kaelen is forced to kill Anora in order to defeat the ghost.
The three remaining party members begin filing back to Stirling's Reach each with a different version of events to report.

Charter of the Wilderlands
    –Issued under authority of Countess Alania Elmander, County of Arnestal
    –Approved by King Faris of Casdenia and the royal council of Casdenia.
    –Lawful, rightful duty to settle in the Wilderlands west of the Highland Mountains
    –Leading council styled as the Warden Protectors of the Wilderlands
    –All who settle shall have tenure and possess claim to their homestead
    –Every right to defend oneself, bearing weapons and building fortifications
    –Provisional laws for local region allowed so long as they do not contradict crown laws
    –Provisional vassalage given to Countess Alania Elmander and the County of Arnestal
    –Exempt from taxes and tithes for a period of two years
    –Status of vassalage to be negotiated and formally established after period of five years
    –Charter negotiation contingent upon successful establishment of settlement 
    –Must maintain provisional military force and meet military obligations
    –Must report sightings of enemy, heresies, or foreign spy activities
    –Revocation of charter if Warden-Protector(s) are guilty of treason or tyranny
    –Revocation of charter if settlement abandoned or surrendered
